metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after low points) and overestimates downward corrections.
- Forecasts tend to lag by 1–3 days in reacting to true price spikes or drops; adjust for recent volatility.
- After a spike (e.g., >40), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecasted values at +10% above peak or below -10% from trough.
- Mean reversion is weak in early forecast horizon (1–7 days); model should not assume trend continuation unless sentiment is strongly bullish/bearish.
- Sentiment history is flat (0.00) in all examples — model should not ignore sentiment when it becomes non-zero; if sentiment > 0.2, increase forecast bias toward bullish; if < -0.2, bias toward bearish.
- Horizon-specific error: 10–14 day forecasts are most prone to overestimating volatility; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% for longer horizons.
- If true outcome shows a “double dip” or “V-shaped” correction, model should not predict a flat recovery — instead, forecast a 2–3 day dip before rebound.
